artifacts.notes:
Links 21 PDFs: the Liturgy of the Word bookmark, Eucharistic Prayers I-IV for
concelebration, two parallel-text comparisons, twelve Order of Mass leaflets in a
four-by-three grid of content against format, and the pocket Order of Mass. It
also links a separate Holy Week and Triduum page. Its Saint Joseph paragraph
reads: "In 2013 The Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the
Sacraments have informed Bishops' Conferences that henceforward St Joseph is to
be inserted into Eucharistic Prayers II-IV in the Roman Missal."
artifacts.rights_basis:
The index page carries no reuse grant over itself; it carries "(c) CBCEW" and a
bounded grant over the leaflets it links. It is registered because it is the page
that states the delivery terms of the sibling PDFs, names each file, and
announces on its own face the 2013 Saint Joseph emendation that three of those
files predate. The exact bytes are identified and hashed; no payload is retained.

artifacts.notes: File Lords-Entrance.pdf, 12 pp. Listed on Missal/Text/Triduum.shtml as "Palm Sunday - Commemoration of the Lord's Entrance". Palm Sunday, the Commemoration of the Lord's Entrance into Jerusalem: the Address, both Blessing prayers, the Invitation, Procession Antiphons 1 and 2 with their psalms, the Hymn to Christ the King and the Responsory at the entrance into the church, page-numbered to the Missal. IT STOPS AT THE SECOND FORM and does not carry the Third Form's Simple Entrance antiphon. IT ALSO PRINTS PSALM 23 AND PSALM 46 ENTIRE AND CARRIES NO REVISED GRAIL NOTICE -- only ICEL and a Revised Standard Version notice for the procession Gospels -- while the ICEL Antiphonary prints the same psalms and does carry one. Two conference-published documents, the same psalms, different attribution: a rights position may not be inferred from whether a notice appears on the file in hand. Carries "Excerpts from the English translation and chants of The Roman Missal (c) 2010, International Commission on English in the Liturgy Corporation. All rights reserved."

artifacts.notes: File LY-Composers-Guide.pdf, 28 pp. Listed on Missal/Music/Composing/index.shtml as "The Liturgical Year - A Guide for Composers". The Department for Christian Life and Worship's guide to the texts of the Liturgical Year for composers, approved November 2011. It prints texts the other files here do not: Ash Wednesday, the Palm Sunday SIMPLE ENTRANCE ANTIPHON that Lords-Entrance.pdf omits, the Washing of Feet antiphons, the Adoration of the Cross including the Improperia entire and Crucem tuam, the Lucernarium, both Exsultet forms, the Litany, the Blessing of Water, the Sprinkling, and the Presentation of the Lord. Its paragraph 123 states that at the transfer of the Blessed Sacrament "The Missal does not provide any texts at this point but notes that the hymn Pange, lingua or another eucharistic chant is sung" -- which bears on whether two slots in this repository's Holy Week ledger are text slots at all. Carries its own approval line and "Text (c) Bishops' Conference of England & Wales" beside "Excerpts from the English translation and chants of The Roman Missal (c) 2010, International Commission on English in the Liturgy Corporation. All rights reserved."

edition.authority: Published by the Liturgy Office of the Bishops' Conference of England and Wales; the composers' guides carry the approval of its Department for Christian Life and Worship. The English translation is ICEL's.
edition.jurisdiction: England and Wales. THE UNIVERSAL ICEL TEXT IS COMMON TO ICEL'S ELEVEN MEMBER CONFERENCES AND A NATIONAL ADAPTATION IS NOT. Where a text here is the universal ICEL English, this edition witnesses it; where it is an England-and-Wales adaptation, disposition or spelling, this edition witnesses England and Wales and NOT the United States, and nothing here may be carried onto a United States surface without that being established element by element.
edition.notes:
Registered as an English edition line of the Missal because these files print
Missal text, but the container is CBCEW's: the leaflets carry "Compilation &
layout (c) 2011 Catholic Bishops' Conference of England and Wales", the
composers' guides carry "Text (c) 2010, 2011 Bishops' Conference of England &
Wales" and their own approval line, and the Liturgy Office's Missal pages carry
"(c) CBCEW". Two properties in one file, always. A fuller work record for the
composers' guides as CBCEW documents in their own right is open work and belongs
to a lane that owns a CBCEW namespace; this lane does not.

FOUR CAUTIONS ESTABLISHED BY OPENING THE FILES, not inferred.

AS OF WHEN. EP2-A4.pdf, EP3-A4.pdf and EP4-A4.pdf were produced on 1 September
2011 and none of the three contains the name of Saint Joseph, which the
Congregation for Divine Worship directed be inserted into Eucharistic Prayers
II-IV in 2013 -- a change the Liturgy Office's own Text page announces on its
face while continuing to serve these files. They are an accurate witness to the
2011 state and a wrong witness to the present one.

FILES THAT CARRY NO ACKNOWLEDGMENT. EP1-A4.pdf, EP2-A4.pdf, EP3-A4.pdf,
EP4-A4.pdf and Word-bookmark.pdf carry no copyright notice anywhere in their
bytes. Condition (2) of ICEL's clause requires the appropriate acknowledgment,
and a file that does not carry one cannot supply it; take the wording from
ICEL's copyright page and from the sibling files that do carry it.

SUPERSEDED TEXT PRINTED DELIBERATELY. Compare-2-Peoples.pdf and
Compare-3-Peoples.pdf print the 1973 translation in parallel with the 2010, and
their notices claim both. The 1973 English is ICEL's and is NOT promulgated text
anywhere in the English-speaking world; ICEL's web clause reaches texts that
have been approved, recognised AND promulgated, so the 1973 column is outside it
and must never be lifted as Missal text.

A FILE THAT IS NOT A TEXT. Initiation.pdf is a comparative table of the
RCIA/Missal ritual pathways, not a liturgical text, and carries a CBCEW notice
rather than an ICEL one.

passages.context:
The Liturgy Office's own terms over the files it publishes, read on 2026-08-21
from the retained bytes. Immediately above the table of Order of Mass leaflets:

"The following leaflets may be reproduced for local parish use."

and at the foot of the page, as on every Missal page of the site:

"(c) CBCEW"

RECORDED SO THAT THE TWO LAYERS ARE NOT RUN TOGETHER. This is the delivery
publisher's grant over its own compilation and typography, and it is bounded to
local parish use. It does not reach a permanent website, it is not the basis on
which ICEL text appears on this project's pages, and it is the reason the
sibling artifacts are stored remote with no payload retained. The basis for
publishing the ICEL text those files carry is ICEL's own Global Computer
Networks clause, recorded at
passage.international-commission-on-english-in-the-liturgy.publication-policies.2013-amended-booklet.global-computer-networks.

The same page states the intent behind the leaflets -- "the Order of Mass in a
format which can be copied and used as a participation aid" -- which is worth
noticing for a different reason. A participation aid is a regulated publication
category under the USCCB's 2025 guidelines and its equivalents; this project is
not one and must not become one by imitating these leaflets' function.

The page's own Saint Joseph paragraph is the dated correction that its
Eucharistic Prayer files do not carry: "In 2013 The Congregation for Divine
Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments have informed Bishops' Conferences
that henceforward St Joseph is to be inserted into Eucharistic Prayers II-IV in
the Roman Missal." EP2-A4.pdf, EP3-A4.pdf and EP4-A4.pdf were produced on 1
September 2011 and contain no occurrence of the name.
passages.notes: The parallel Holy Week page, /Missal/Text/Triduum.shtml, describes its excerpts as "intended for printing and insertion in a worthy folder for use in the liturgy" -- the same bounded, print-and-parish sense of the grant.

passages.rights_basis:
The index page carries no reuse grant over itself; it carries "(c) CBCEW" and a
bounded grant over the leaflets it links. It is registered because it is the page
that states the delivery terms of the sibling PDFs, names each file, and
announces on its own face the 2013 Saint Joseph emendation that three of those
files predate. The exact bytes are identified and hashed; no payload is retained.
